name: Samrat Choudhary
role: Chief minister of Bihar (2026–); former deputy chief minister and state BJP leader
summary: Choudhary promotes welfare delivery, industrial investment and employment alongside stronger policing and continued liquor prohibition. He supports a uniform civil code and a cow-slaughter ban, has endorsed investigations framed around love jihad, and defends caste reservations through constitutional channels.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Explicitly promises to ban cow slaughter if his party governs Bihar.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Insists that the people’s electoral verdict must be respected, including when his party loses.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Responds to the court’s quota ruling with a constitutional appeal rather than claiming immunity from judicial review.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Defends cash assistance, pensions and subsidized electricity as delivered public commitments.

democracy-best.rationale: Says voters are the ultimate authority and explicitly accepts his party’s by-election defeat.

dynastic-succession.rationale: He repeatedly criticises Lalu Prasad for passing power to Rabri Devi and then Tejashwi, saying social justice does not mean someone becomes king and JP stood for people's power, not one-family rule; he contrasts this with his party's rotation of leaders.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Says every caste contributes to society and supports benefits without religious discrimination.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Explicitly includes atomic-power development in his employment and industrial plans.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Mixed: he says Bihar does not stage direct encounters, only answers fire and sends suspects to speedy trial, and ordered a judicial inquiry into the Bharat Tiwari encounter, yet he also tells police to answer any challenge within 48 hours, warns criminals to leave Bihar or go to the crematorium, and over a dozen encounters followed; none of this is specific to drug suspects.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: He cites with approval Bihar's 50 percent reservation for women in local leadership (and credits the NDA government with creating it for women and EBCs in panchayats), noting that women now win about 59 percent of those seats.

harm-principle.rationale: Defends blanket liquor prohibition as a social protection policy.

job-guarantee.rationale: Says government jobs are limited; relies primarily on industrial employment.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Supports prohibition, dedicated anti-drug units and enforcement campaigns.

local-production.rationale: Requires local procurement and promotes Bihar-based manufacturing.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Promises to investigate alleged love-jihad cases, accepting a framing of organized conversion through relationships; the allegations are not established facts.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: He treats Bihar's large population as a demographic advantage and blames the state's backwardness and migration on years of misrule, lost industry and revenue, not on population growth.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Presents completion of the Ram temple as a fulfilled public aspiration, then stresses development.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Defends support for poor families as a legitimate use of public revenue.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Ordered police action against songs insulting entire castes.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Emphasizes delivery and governance outcomes and defends working with a former rival for development.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Ordered an independent judicial probe into a disputed police killing, while promoting a tough encounter-oriented policing model.

separated-powers.rationale: Defends independent courts and says he will not interfere with judicial examination of recruitment complaints.

social-market-economy.rationale: Combines support for private industrial enterprise with extensive public welfare and subsidies.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Uses subsidized land and incentives to attract strategic industries.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: He says the 125 free units go to every household without checking whether the recipient is Lalu Yadav or a poor person; he only invites those who can afford it to give up the benefit voluntarily, which does not make it targeted. (His more recent position; earlier he defended grants for poor families.)

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Promises a UCC bill after consultation with coalition partners.

notes:
Read full interviews from 2024, 2025 and September 2026, examined earlier religious campaign pledges and current policing controversies, and checked every one of the 490 statements. Policies explicitly defended in his interviews count as his; his party’s national manifesto and other leaders’ policies do not automatically count. Caste reservations are not assumed to be racial preferences, and proportional representation of castes is not proportional allocation of legislative seats by party vote. Investigating alleged coercive conversion does not establish a general ban on voluntary conversion or interfaith marriage. Religious observance and support for one temple do not establish scriptural law, clerical rule or a religious test for citizenship. The police inquiry is recorded alongside the encounter controversy; tough policing is not converted into approval of killing suspected drug offenders without trial. Demolition of alleged encroachments, and his promise to protect lawful owners, do not establish a general doctrine of fundamental property rights. Employment targets combining private and public work are not universal state job guarantees. Flood-control engineering does not itself establish a climate-change policy. The absence of direct positions on most world, ecology and technology statements remains unknown; no inference from party, caste or family.

Merged with an independent claude-sonnet-5-5 audit: 4 answers taken from it, 10 agreed, 1 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: Independent second pass built from long interviews and speeches of his own (Hindi auto-captions read directly, plus 2022-2023 Indian Express interviews) rather than the Organiser and Idea Exchange pieces the first audit used. Themes searched: economy (industrial, welfare, subsidies, budget), liberty (prohibition, drugs, police, encounters), government (dynasty, democracy, courts, panchayat reservation), culture, technology and nuclear power, world (Farakka and the Bangladesh water treaty, Operation Sindoor, infiltrators), ecology, society. Cattle slaughter, conversion law, UCC, hate speech and caste reservation could not be settled from the new sources: on the UCC he said only that Bihar will decide after talks with coalition allies (Panchayat AajTak, Sept 2026), which is not a stated position either way. Caste reservation is not answered on the race-based statements; the Bihar caste survey he called incomplete, which is not a position on any statement. Translations from Hindi are mine, and auto-captions carry no speaker labels, so each passage was used only where the chief minister is plainly the one answering. Policies count as his where he drove or defended them in his own words; the Centre's and allies' positions do not. 'Encounter' record: more than a dozen police encounters under his government (ETV Bharat), balanced by his own stated rejection of direct encounters and the judicial inquiry he ordered, so extrajudicial-killing stays 0 at low.
